claims.text: The target material is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can be used to calculate the melting temperature of refractory high-entropy alloys.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the entropy of fusion of refractory high-entropy alloys.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the enthalpy of fusion of refractory high-entropy alloys.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the volume change at the melting point of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The ab initio DFT free-energy approach can accurately predict melting properties.
The approach accounts for complex interactions among the different elements in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Accounting for complex interelement interactions enables accurate prediction of the alloy's melting properties.
The ab initio free-energy approach has a high computational cost.
The computational cost may limit the approach's applicability to high-throughput calculations.
Comparison with experimental measurements can be used to evaluate the predicted melting properties.
A significant deviation between predicted and experimentally measured melting properties would falsify the hypothesis.
